# API Reference



API Reference [#api-reference]

This page documents the package spine first: the singletons, DTOs, and configuration surfaces most apps touch immediately.

For backend endpoint inspection, use the live OpenAPI surface at [rhea-tribunal.fly.dev/swagger](https://rhea-tribunal.fly.dev/swagger/).

Core singletons [#core-singletons]

`RheaAPI` [#rheaapi]

```swift
public final class RheaAPI: @unchecked Sendable {
    public static let shared: RheaAPI

    public func get(_ path: String, auth: Bool = false) async throws -> Data
    public func post(_ path: String, body: Encodable, auth: Bool = true) async throws -> Data
    public func getJSON(_ path: String, auth: Bool = false) async throws -> [String: Any]

    public func health() async throws -> HealthSnapshot
    public func agents() async throws -> [AgentDTO]
    public func history(limit: Int = 50) async throws -> [[String: Any]]
    public func radio(limit: Int = 100) async throws -> [[String: Any]]
    public func office(limit: Int = 50) async throws -> [[String: Any]]
    public func proofs() async throws -> [[String: Any]]
    public func ontologies() async throws -> [[String: Any]]
    public func ontologyDetail(_ name: String) async throws -> [[String: Any]]
    public func models() async throws -> InfraModels
    public func ndi() async throws -> [String: Any]
    public func sessions(limit: Int = 20) async throws -> [[String: Any]]

    public func walletStatus() async throws -> [[String: Any]]
    public func walletBalance(chain: String) async throws -> [String: Any]

    public func supervisorSessions() async throws -> [SupervisorSession]
    public func supervisorSpawn(agent: String, prompt: String? = nil) async throws -> [String: Any]
    public func supervisorKill(sessionId: String) async throws -> [String: Any]
    public func supervisorOutput(sessionId: String, lines: Int = 50) async throws -> String
    public func supervisorInput(sessionId: String, text: String) async throws -> [String: Any]
    public func wakeAgent(_ agent: String) async throws -> [String: Any]

    public func governorAll() async throws -> [String: GovernorAgentStatus]
    public func governor(agent: String) async throws -> GovernorAgentStatus

    public func executionProfile() async throws -> [String: Any]
    public func setExecutionProfile(_ profile: String) async throws -> [String: Any]

    public func ndiDiscover() async throws -> [NDISource]
    public func ndiSendTest() async throws -> [String: Any]

    public var apiKey: String { get }
    public func setAPIKey(_ key: String)
    public var baseURL: String { get }
}
```

`RheaStore` [#rheastore]

```swift
@MainActor
public final class RheaStore: ObservableObject {
    public static let shared: RheaStore

    @Published public var agents: [AgentDTO]
    @Published public var health: HealthSnapshot?
    @Published public var connectionAlive: Bool
    @Published public var proofCount: Int

    public var totalTokens: Int
    public var totalCost: Double
    public var aliveCount: Int
    public var familyOnline: Bool

    public private(set) var agentMap: OrderedDictionary<String, AgentDTO>

    public func startPolling(interval: TimeInterval = 5)
    public func stopPolling()
    public func refreshCore() async

    public func refreshHistory(limit: Int = 50) async -> [[String: Any]]
    public func refreshRadio(limit: Int = 100) async -> [[String: Any]]
    public func refreshProofs() async -> [[String: Any]]
    public func refreshOntologies() async -> [[String: Any]]
    public func refreshOffice(limit: Int = 50) async -> [[String: Any]]
    public func refreshSessions(limit: Int = 20) async -> [[String: Any]]

    public func age(_ key: String) -> TimeInterval
    public func formatTokens(_ n: Int) -> String
    public let db: DatabaseQueue?
}
```

`AuthManager` [#authmanager]

```swift
public class AuthManager: ObservableObject {
    public static let shared: AuthManager

    @Published public var token: String?
    @Published public var email: String?
    @Published public var plan: String
    @Published public var queriesUsed: Int
    @Published public var queryLimit: Int
    @Published public var didSkipAuth: Bool

    public var isLoggedIn: Bool

    public func save(token: String, email: String)
    public func logout()
    public func skipLogin()
    public func authorize(_ request: inout URLRequest)
}
```

Key DTOs [#key-dtos]

`AgentDTO` [#agentdto]

```swift
public struct AgentDTO: Codable, Identifiable {
    public let name: String
    public let alive: Bool
    public let pace: String
    public let mode: String
    public let billing_mode: String?
    public let T_day: Int
    public let dollar_day: Double
    public let floor_gap: Int
    public let office_status: String?
    public let pending_msgs: Int?
    public let tasks_open: Int?
    public let tasks_claimed: Int?
    public let last_activity: String?
    public let last_feed: String?
    public let lease_token: Int?
    public let lease_expired: Bool?
    public let lease_expires_at: String?
    public let forecast: String?
    public let budget_cap: Double?
    public let budget_remaining: Double?
    public let hard_fail: Bool?
}
```

`HealthSnapshot` [#healthsnapshot]

```swift
public struct HealthSnapshot: Codable {
    public let status: String
    public let providers_available: Int
    public let providers_total: Int
    public let total_models: Int
    public let execution_profile: String
    public let analyzer_version: String
    public let profile_mode: String
}
```

Other exported surface types [#other-exported-surface-types]

| Type                  | Role                                           |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `SupervisorSession`   | Supervisor session identity and runtime status |
| `GovernorAgentStatus` | Pace, forecast, budget cap, and compliance     |
| `InfraModels`         | Provider and model inventory                   |
| `NDISource`           | Discoverable NDI source metadata               |
| `TaskItem`            | Task management row payload                    |
| `FeedItem`            | Team radio message payload                     |
| `ChatMsg`             | Dialog history message                         |
| `PipelineNode`        | Node editor graph node                         |
| `NodeType`            | Graph node variant enum                        |


```swift
public enum RheaTheme {
```

# Architecture



Architecture [#architecture]

RheaKit uses a layered architecture: views observe shared state, shared state is fed by a single API client, and the API client handles transport and authentication concerns.

Layer diagram [#layer-diagram]

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SwiftUI Views                     │
│  TeamChat · Governor · Tasks · Bio · Dialog · ...   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    RheaStore                         │
│  @MainActor · @Published · GRDB local cache         │
│  Polling: agents, health, proofCount (every 5s)     │
│  On-demand: history, radio, proofs, ontologies      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    RheaAPI                           │
│  Singleton HTTP client · URLSession                 │
│  JWT Bearer + API-key fallback · Typed DTOs         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                   AuthManager                        │
│  Keychain-backed JWT · Sign in with Apple           │
│  Skip-login mode for dev · Profile fetch            │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                  Rhea Backend                        │
│  Fly.io (prod) · localhost:8400 (dev)               │
│  SQL-backed endpoints · In-memory governor state    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

`RheaStore`: the shared brain [#rheastore-the-shared-brain]

`RheaStore` is a `@MainActor` singleton `ObservableObject` and the package source of truth.

Data tiers [#data-tiers]

| Tier      | What                                                 | Refresh                     |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Core      | Agents, health, proof count                          | Automatic five-second timer |
| On-demand | History, radio, proofs, ontologies, sessions, office | Loaded when panes open      |
| Ephemeral | SSE streams, active dialog state                     | Never cached                |

Derived metrics [#derived-metrics]

```swift
var totalTokens: Int
var totalCost: Double
var aliveCount: Int
var familyOnline: Bool
```

Staleness and recovery [#staleness-and-recovery]

Each fetched surface records its last refresh. Views can inspect `store.age("proofs")` before doing expensive work.

When connection returns after an outage, `RheaStore` follows a strict recovery order:

1. Confirm membrane integrity: the backend responds to core agent state.
2. Refill metabolism: refresh SQL-backed surfaces such as proofs, history, radio, and office.
3. Accept hard resets honestly: in-memory governor counters may reset to zero after restart.
4. Resume normal polling.

`RheaAPI`: transport and typed endpoints [#rheaapi-transport-and-typed-endpoints]

`RheaAPI` hides raw URLSession calls behind narrow methods that map to real backend capabilities.

| Method                 | Endpoint                   | Returns                         |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `health()`             | `GET /health`              | `HealthSnapshot`                |
| `agents()`             | `GET /agents/status`       | `[AgentDTO]`                    |
| `history()`            | `GET /cc/history`          | `[[String: Any]]`               |
| `radio()`              | `GET /cc/radio`            | `[[String: Any]]`               |
| `proofs()`             | `GET /aletheia/proofs`     | `[[String: Any]]`               |
| `ontologies()`         | `GET /ontology`            | `[[String: Any]]`               |
| `models()`             | `GET /models`              | `InfraModels`                   |
| `sessions()`           | `GET /cc/sessions`         | `[[String: Any]]`               |
| `walletStatus()`       | `GET /wallet/status`       | `[[String: Any]]`               |
| `governorAll()`        | `GET /governor`            | `[String: GovernorAgentStatus]` |
| `supervisorSessions()` | `GET /supervisor/sessions` | `[SupervisorSession]`           |

Error handling [#error-handling]

```swift
public enum RheaAPIError: Error {
    case invalidURL(String)
    case http(Int, String)
    case decode(String)
}
```

`AppConfig`: environment routing [#appconfig-environment-routing]

RheaKit chooses the backend automatically:

| Environment | API URL                         | Atlas URL               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Simulator   | `http://localhost:8400`         | `http://localhost:3000` |
| Device      | `https://rhea-tribunal.fly.dev` | same host               |

`migrateStaleDefaults()` replaces saved localhost values when an older dev build lands on a real device.

Local cache [#local-cache]

`RheaStore` maintains a GRDB-backed SQLite cache for offline access.

```sql
CREATE TABLE cached_proofs (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    claim TEXT NOT NULL,
    tier TEXT,
    agreement_score REAL,
    confidence REAL,
    created_at TEXT,
    data TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE cached_history (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    prompt TEXT NOT NULL,
    agreement_score REAL,
    created_at TEXT,
    data TEXT
);
```

This mirrors the server's durable data, while keeping ephemeral operational surfaces refresh-driven.

Architectural bias [#architectural-bias]

RheaKit deliberately avoids duplicated fetchers and locally improvised caches in individual panes. If you need data in a new view, either add it to the store or make the view explicitly on-demand. Silent shadow state is the fast path to impossible debugging.


# Design System



Design System [#design-system]

RheaKit's visual language is defined in `RheaTheme`: one set of tokens for background, emphasis, operational state, and severity. It is deliberately dark-first and data-forward.

Color palette [#color-palette]

| Token        | Value                | Usage                        |
| ------------ | -------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `bg`         | `rgb(15, 15, 26)`    | Primary background           |
| `card`       | `rgb(26, 26, 41)`    | Panel surface                |
| `cardBorder` | `white @ 6%`         | Subtle panel outline         |
| `accent`     | `rgb(102, 217, 255)` | Primary interactive cyan     |
| `green`      | `rgb(77, 230, 128)`  | Healthy, live, success       |
| `amber`      | `rgb(255, 199, 51)`  | Warning, compact, degraded   |
| `red`        | `rgb(255, 89, 89)`   | Error, critical, blocked     |
| `purple`     | `rgb(179, 128, 255)` | Proof and hard-fail emphasis |
| `muted`      | `white @ 50%`        | Secondary text               |
| `text`       | `white`              | Primary text                 |

```swift
Text("Online")
    .foregroundStyle(RheaTheme.green)

Text("3 alerts")
    .foregroundStyle(RheaTheme.red)

Rectangle()
    .fill(RheaTheme.bg)
```

Semantic color functions [#semantic-color-functions]

`modeColor(_ mode: String) -> Color` [#modecolor_-mode-string---color]

| Mode        | Color  |
| ----------- | ------ |
| `normal`    | green  |
| `compact`   | amber  |
| `critical`  | red    |
| `hard_fail` | purple |

`paceColor(_ pace: String) -> Color` [#pacecolor_-pace-string---color]

| Pace     | Color |
| -------- | ----- |
| `green`  | green |
| `yellow` | amber |
| `red`    | red   |

`priorityColor(_ priority: String) -> Color` [#prioritycolor_-priority-string---color]

| Priority | Color  |
| -------- | ------ |
| `P0`     | red    |
| `P1`     | amber  |
| `P2`     | accent |

`statusColor(_ status: String) -> Color` [#statuscolor_-status-string---color]

| Status    | Color     |
| --------- | --------- |
| `open`    | secondary |
| `claimed` | accent    |
| `done`    | green     |
| `blocked` | red       |

GlassCard [#glasscard]

`.glassCard()` is the package's signature shell for compact, dense information surfaces.

```swift
VStack {
    Text("Agent: Rex")
    Text("Tokens: 12K")
}
.glassCard()
```

Implementation:

```swift
public struct GlassCard: ViewModifier {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .padding(16)
            .background(
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16)
                    .fill(RheaTheme.card)
                    .overlay(
                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16)
                            .stroke(RheaTheme.cardBorder, lineWidth: 1)
                    )
            )
    }
}
```

Typography posture [#typography-posture]

RheaKit does not hide behind decorative type. It uses monospaced data presentation to keep numbers, pace, and status legible under load.

| Context                  | Font pattern                                            |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Section headers          | `.system(size: 10, weight: .bold, design: .monospaced)` |
| Body and payload content | `.system(size: 12, design: .monospaced)`                |
| Badges and status pills  | `.system(size: 9, weight: .bold, design: .monospaced)`  |
| Tiny indicators          | `.system(size: 8-9, design: .monospaced)`               |

Design rules that matter in practice [#design-rules-that-matter-in-practice]

1. Every visible status color must map back to a real state field.
2. Every number shown in a card must have a refresh or provenance path.
3. Decorative panels are allowed, but they cannot outrank the primary action or the current risk signal.
4. Zero after restart is not a bug if the source of truth is in-memory governor state. The UI should treat that zero as truth, not as loss.

Where to go next [#where-to-go-next]

# Getting Started



Getting Started [#getting-started]

RheaKit is a Swift Package. The fastest route in is: add the package, set the backend base URL, boot the shared store, then mount the views you actually need.

Requirements [#requirements]

| Requirement | Version |
| ----------- | ------- |
| Swift       | 5.9+    |
| iOS         | 17.0+   |
| macOS       | 14.0+   |
| Xcode       | 15.0+   |

1\. Add the package [#1-add-the-package]

In your app's `Package.swift`, add RheaKit as a dependency:

```swift
// Package.swift
let package = Package(
    name: "MyApp",
    platforms: [.iOS(.v17), .macOS(.v14)],
    dependencies: [
        .package(path: "../packages/RheaKit"),
    ],
    targets: [
        .executableTarget(
            name: "MyApp",
            dependencies: ["RheaKit"]
        ),
    ]
)
```

If you prefer Xcode:

1. Open `File -> Add Package Dependencies...`
2. Point Xcode at the Rhea repository or the package folder
3. Select the branch or revision you want to ship against

2\. Confirm the backend target [#2-confirm-the-backend-target]

RheaKit automatically distinguishes between simulator and device:

| Runtime   | Default API URL                 |
| --------- | ------------------------------- |
| Simulator | `http://localhost:8400`         |
| Device    | `https://rhea-tribunal.fly.dev` |

You can override it with `UserDefaults`:

```swift
import RheaKit

UserDefaults.standard.set(
    "https://your-server.example.com",
    forKey: "apiBaseURL"
)
```

At launch, call:

```swift
AppConfig.migrateStaleDefaults()
```

That migrates older localhost values off physical devices so you do not strand a production build on an unreachable dev host.

3\. Start the shared state spine [#3-start-the-shared-state-spine]

`RheaStore` is the package nerve cord. It owns the core polling loop and recovery logic.

```swift
import SwiftUI
import RheaKit

@main
struct MyApp: App {
    init() {
        AppConfig.migrateStaleDefaults()
        RheaStore.shared.startPolling()
    }

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            ContentView()
        }
    }
}
```

The store polls `/agents/status` and `/health` every five seconds, then refreshes heavier SQL-backed surfaces on demand.

4\. Gate the app with auth [#4-gate-the-app-with-auth]

RheaKit uses `AuthManager.shared` for JWT state. A user can authenticate or skip, depending on your product policy.

```swift
import RheaKit

struct ContentView: View {
    @ObservedObject private var auth = AuthManager.shared

    var body: some View {
        if auth.isLoggedIn || auth.didSkipAuth {
            MainTabView()
        } else {
            AuthView()
        }
    }
}
```

`AuthView` already includes sign-in, sign-up, and Apple Sign In plumbing.

5\. Render the first control surfaces [#5-render-the-first-control-surfaces]

Every pane is self-contained. Drop the ones you need into a `TabView` or mount them individually.

```swift
import RheaKit

struct MainTabView: View {
    var body: some View {
        TabView {
            TeamChatView()
                .tabItem { Label("Radio", systemImage: "antenna.radiowaves.left.and.right") }

            GovernorView()
                .tabItem { Label("Governor", systemImage: "gauge.with.dots.needle.67percent") }

            TasksView()
                .tabItem { Label("Tasks", systemImage: "checklist") }

            BioRendererView()
                .tabItem { Label("Bio", systemImage: "atom") }

            SettingsView()
                .tabItem { Label("Settings", systemImage: "gear") }
        }
        .preferredColorScheme(.dark)
    }
}
```

6\. Use the package visual language [#6-use-the-package-visual-language]

Use `RheaTheme` tokens and `.glassCard()` for your own custom panes so they read as native Rhea surfaces.

```swift
import RheaKit

struct MyDashboard: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
            Text("Status: Online")
                .foregroundStyle(RheaTheme.green)

            Text("Queries today: 42")
                .foregroundStyle(RheaTheme.accent)
        }
        .glassCard()
        .background(RheaTheme.bg)
    }
}
```

# AletheiaView



AletheiaView [#aletheiaview]

AletheiaView is the proof store and ontology browser. It exposes immutable tribunal proofs and the hypothesis spaces around them.

Usage [#usage]

```swift
import RheaKit

struct AletheiaTab: View {
    var body: some View {
        AletheiaView()
    }
}
```

Features [#features]

* Proof listing from `/aletheia/proofs`
* Summary badges for proof count and ontology count
* Expandable proof detail for claim, tier, agreement score, and confidence
* Ontology list from `/ontology`
* Pull to refresh
* Loading state while data is being fetched

Layout [#layout]

```text
┌─ Summary Badges ──────────────────┐
│  PROOFS: 42    ONTOLOGIES: 3      │
├───────────────────────────────────┤
│  [Proof Detail — if selected]     │
├───────────────────────────────────┤
│  Proof List                       │
│  ├─ claim: "X is true"           │
│  │  tier: cheap | score: 0.87    │
│  ├─ claim: "Y holds"             │
│  │  tier: mid  | score: 0.92     │
│  └─ ...                          │
├───────────────────────────────────┤
│  Ontology Section                 │
│  ├─ biochemistry                  │
│  ├─ chronobiology                 │
│  └─ ...                          │
└───────────────────────────────────┘
```

Data source [#data-source]

* Proofs via `RheaAPI.shared.proofs()` -> `GET /aletheia/proofs`
* Ontologies via `RheaAPI.shared.ontologies()` -> `GET /ontology`

Notes [#notes]

* Proofs are durable truth records once written to `proof.db`
* The view is iOS-compatible and stays within `NavigationStack`
* A proof record includes `id`, `claim`, `tier`, `agreement_score`, `confidence`, and `created_at`


# BioRendererView



BioRendererView [#biorendererview]

BioRendererView is a 3D molecular visualization surface powered by [3Dmol.js](https://3dmol.csb.pitt.edu/) inside a `WKWebView`. It supports PDB lookup, SMILES input, multiple rendering styles, and tribunal-backed analysis.

Usage [#usage]

```swift
import RheaKit

struct MoleculeTab: View {
    var body: some View {
        BioRendererView()
    }
}
```

The view is self-contained. Drop it into a `TabView` or present it modally.

Features [#features]

* PDB lookup from RCSB
* SMILES mode for small molecules
* Cartoon, stick, sphere, line, and cross rendering
* Spectrum, chain, secondary structure, element, and residue color schemes
* Touch and mouse interaction
* Preset molecules for rapid demos and testing
* Analysis panel that forwards the active structure to the backend
* Metadata display for title, method, resolution, and organism

Presets [#presets]

| PDB ID | Name            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| `1CRN` | Crambin         |
| `1BNA` | DNA B-form      |
| `4HHB` | Hemoglobin      |
| `1ATP` | ATP synthase    |
| `6LU7` | SARS-CoV-2 Mpro |
| `1GZM` | GFP             |

Render styles [#render-styles]

| Style     | Description                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------- |
| `cartoon` | Secondary structure ribbons     |
| `stick`   | Ball-and-stick bonds            |
| `sphere`  | Space-filling CPK spheres       |
| `line`    | Wireframe bonds                 |
| `cross`   | Cross markers at atom positions |

Notes [#notes]

* `3Dmol-min.js` is bundled locally, so rendering does not depend on a CDN
* PDB files come from RCSB
* Visualization is client-side; only fetch and AI analysis require network


# ClipboardView



ClipboardView [#clipboardview]

ClipboardView manages text, links, and code snippets across devices via the Rhea backend.

Usage [#usage]

```swift
import RheaKit

struct ClipboardTab: View {
    var body: some View {
        ClipboardView()
    }
}
```

Features [#features]

* Push local clipboard content to `POST /clipboard`
* Pull cloud clips back to the local pasteboard
* Auto-poll every five seconds
* Pin and unpin important clips
* Privacy levels: normal, sensitive, secret
* Distinct icons by content type
* Expiry handling and swipe-to-delete

Data model [#data-model]

```swift
struct ClipEntry: Identifiable, Codable {
    let id: String
    let content: String
    let contentType: String
    let contentPreview: String?
    let deviceName: String
    let privacy: String
    let pinned: Bool
    let createdAt: String
    let expiresAt: String?
}
```

Privacy levels [#privacy-levels]

| Level       | Badge | Behavior                                           |
| ----------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `normal`    | —     | Full content visible and copyable                  |
| `sensitive` | 🔒    | Content remains visible but marked                 |
| `secret`    | 🔐    | Only the preview is shown; tap-to-copy is disabled |

Notes [#notes]

* Device name is auto-detected from the host platform
* Auth uses JWT bearer with a dev fallback key when available
* URL content is auto-detected from the pasted string


# DialogView



DialogView [#dialogview]

DialogView is the conversational surface over the tribunal. Every prompt goes through the multi-model consensus engine instead of a single raw model response.

Usage [#usage]

```swift
import RheaKit

struct ChatTab: View {
    var body: some View {
        DialogView()
    }
}
```

Features [#features]

* Tribunal-backed responses
* Markdown rendering via `MarkdownUI`
* Conversation history from `GET /cc/dialog`
* Agreement score, models responded, and elapsed time metadata
* Distinct presentation for human and AI messages

Core data models [#core-data-models]

```swift
public struct ChatMsg: Codable, Identifiable {
    public let id: String
    public let sender: String
    public let text: String
    public let ts: String

    public var isHuman: Bool
    public var displayTime: String
}
```

```swift
public struct DialogResponse: Codable {
    public let reply: String?
    public let agreement_score: Double?
    public let models_responded: Int?
    public let elapsed_s: Double?
    public let ts: String?
}
```

Notes [#notes]

* History is SQL-backed and survives backend restarts
* Auto-scroll uses `ScrollViewReader`
* This is the right pane when you need operator dialogue plus verification signal, not just raw chat


# GovernorView



GovernorView [#governorview]

GovernorView is the budget and pace dashboard for the agent system. It turns token burn, cost, pace, and floor-gap pressure into a readable control surface.

Usage [#usage]

```swift
import RheaKit

struct GovernorTab: View {
    var body: some View {
        GovernorView()
    }
}
```

Features [#features]

* Swift Charts line graph for token burn over the last five minutes
* Summary header with total tokens, cost, and live agent counts
* Agent cards with pace, mode, tokens, cost, and floor gap
* Auto-polling from `/agents/status`
* Pull to refresh

Agent fields displayed [#agent-fields-displayed]

| Field              | Meaning                                 |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `alive`            | whether the agent is responding         |
| `pace`             | green, yellow, or red burn state        |
| `mode`             | normal, compact, critical, or hard-fail |
| `T_day`            | tokens consumed today                   |
| `dollar_day`       | total spend today                       |
| `floor_gap`        | distance from minimum required floor    |
| `forecast`         | budget or exhaustion forecast           |
| `budget_cap`       | maximum daily budget                    |
| `budget_remaining` | remaining budget                        |

Notes [#notes]

* The chart keeps up to 60 points, which covers roughly five minutes at the default cadence
* If the backend restarts and governor counters reset, zero is treated as truth, not silent interpolation


# Components



Components [#components]

RheaKit is not a bag of small widgets. It ships opinionated, full-screen control surfaces that assume a real backend, real state, and real operator intent.

Primary documented surfaces [#primary-documented-surfaces]

<Cards>
  <Card title="BioRendererView" href="./bio-renderer">
    3Dmol.js-powered molecular rendering in a native SwiftUI shell.
  </Card>

  <Card title="NodeEditorView" href="./node-editor">
    Construct tribunal workflows visually with typed nodes and execution state.
  </Card>

  <Card title="TeamChatView" href="./team-chat">
    Live inter-agent radio feed with filtering, send mode, and wake controls.
  </Card>

  <Card title="ClipboardView" href="./clipboard">
    Cross-device clipboard flows with privacy levels, pinning, and expiry.
  </Card>

  <Card title="DialogView" href="./dialog">
    Tribunal-backed conversational interface with agreement and timing metadata.
  </Card>

  <Card title="GovernorView" href="./governor">
    Track spend, burn, mode, pace, and floor-gap pressure in real time.
  </Card>

  <Card title="TasksView" href="./tasks">
    Kanban-style task operations across the multi-agent system.
  </Card>

  <Card title="AletheiaView" href="./aletheia">
    Proof browsing, immutable verification state, and ontology inventory.
  </Card>

  <Card title="ProcessesView" href="./processes">
    Spawn, inspect, and control supervisor-backed sessions.
  </Card>

  <Card title="PulseMonitorView" href="./pulse-monitor">
    Lease state, queue health, and pulse-level ops oversight.
  </Card>
</Cards>

Additional package surfaces already in tree [#additional-package-surfaces-already-in-tree]

The package target currently also contains these files and views:

| Area                         | Current files                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Transport and state          | `RheaAPI`, `RheaStore`, `AppConfig`, `AgentDTO`, `Theme`                                                                                      |
| Auth and privacy             | `AuthView`, `RelayPrivacyView`, `PairingView`, `PairingDelegate`, `DPIView`, `DPIBypassEngine`, `TunnelManager`, `MeshManager`                |
| Research and visualization   | `AtlasWebView`, `MonitorWebView`, `NDIFlowView`, `NetworkFlowerView`, `NetworkFlowerEngine`, `RuliadView`, `BioSvgTemplateEngine`             |
| Operations and utility panes | `OfficeView`, `OpsView`, `ModelsView`, `WalletView`, `HistoryView`, `SettingsView`, `AuthorView`, `MenuBarView`, `ToolsHubView`, `ChainsView` |

Selection rule [#selection-rule]

Start with the surfaces that reveal the system's real state:

1. `GovernorView` if you need risk and spend visibility.
2. `TeamChatView` if you need to see agent traffic.
3. `TasksView` if work coordination is primary.
4. `AletheiaView` if proofs and verification are the product core.
5. `BioRendererView` or `NodeEditorView` when the domain includes interactive science or workflow design.

Do not mount the whole package just because it exists. Pick the minimum set that gives a truthful operator surface.


# NodeEditorView



NodeEditorView [#nodeeditorview]

NodeEditorView is a visual pipeline editor for tribunal workflows. You drag nodes onto a canvas, connect them, configure their parameters, and execute the resulting graph against the backend.

Usage [#usage]

```swift
import RheaKit

struct PipelineTab: View {
    var body: some View {
        NodeEditorView()
    }
}
```

Node types [#node-types]

| Type       | Role                             |
| ---------- | -------------------------------- |
| `input`    | Starting claim or prompt         |
| `tribunal` | Multi-model consensus evaluation |
| `sceptic`  | Adversarial challenge            |
| `filter`   | Threshold gate                   |
| `proof`    | Proof-store commit               |
| `output`   | Final result surface             |

Configuration surface [#configuration-surface]

| Node     | Parameters       |
| -------- | ---------------- |
| Input    | `claim`          |
| Tribunal | `models`, `tier` |
| Sceptic  | `intensity`      |
| Filter   | `threshold`      |
| Proof    | `tag`            |
| Output   | none             |

Backing model [#backing-model]

```swift
public struct PipelineNode: Identifiable, Codable {
    public let id: UUID
    public var type: NodeType
    public var position: CGPoint
    public var connections: [UUID]
    public var config: [String: String]
    public var resultText: String?
}
```

Notes [#notes]

* The canvas supports pan and zoom
* Connections are directional
* Running the graph serializes nodes into a workflow payload and POSTs it to the backend


# ProcessesView



ProcessesView [#processesview]

ProcessesView is the operator pane for supervisor-backed sessions.

Features [#features]

* List active and historical sessions
* Spawn new agents with optional prompts
* Kill sessions with confirmation
* Pull recent output lines
* Send interactive input to a session
* Show running versus stopped counts in the toolbar

Core model [#core-model]

```swift
public struct SupervisorSession: Codable, Identifiable {
    public let id: String
    public let agent: String?
    public let status: String?
    public let started_at: String?
    public let pid: Int?

    public var isAlive: Bool
    public var stateColor: String
}
```

API touchpoints [#api-touchpoints]

| Action        | Endpoint                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| List sessions | `GET /supervisor/sessions`            |
| Spawn         | `POST /supervisor/spawn`              |
| Kill          | `POST /supervisor/kill/:id`           |
| Read output   | `GET /supervisor/output/:id?lines=50` |
| Send input    | `POST /supervisor/input/:id`          |

Notes [#notes]

* Output is fetched on demand, not streamed by default
* Known agent names are exposed in the spawn sheet for fast reuse


# PulseMonitorView



PulseMonitorView [#pulsemonitorview]

PulseMonitorView is the ops-console layer above the agent network. It focuses on queue health, stale work, and lease state rather than conversational flow.

Features [#features]

* Queue summary with totals by status and priority
* Agent pulse cards with lease token and expiry data
* Auto-polling
* Agent filtering shared with TeamChatView preferences

Queue model [#queue-model]

```swift
public struct PulseQueueSummary: Codable {
    public let total: Int
    public let counts: [String: Int]
    public let active_by_priority: [String: Int]
    public let stale_count: Int
    public let _updated: String?
}
```

Lease fields surfaced [#lease-fields-surfaced]

| Field              | Meaning                        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| `lease_token`      | current lease token count      |
| `lease_expired`    | whether the lease is expired   |
| `lease_expires_at` | ISO-8601 expiry timestamp      |
| `office_status`    | office relay state             |
| `pending_msgs`     | unread messages                |
| `tasks_open`       | tasks opened against the agent |
| `tasks_claimed`    | tasks currently claimed        |

Notes [#notes]

* Pulse uses the same `AgentDTO` spine as GovernorView
* It is the correct surface when you need to see queue drift, not budget drift


# TasksView



TasksView [#tasksview]

TasksView is the task coordination pane for the multi-agent system.

Features [#features]

* Status filters for open, claimed, done, and blocked
* Agent and priority filtering
* New task sheet
* Auto-refresh
* Animated card transitions

Task model [#task-model]

```swift
public struct TaskItem: Codable, Identifiable {
    public let id: String
    public let title: String
    public let priority: String
    public let status: String
    public let agent: String
    public let claimed_by: String
    public let tags: [String]
}
```

Color semantics [#color-semantics]

| Priority | Color              |
| -------- | ------------------ |
| `P0`     | `RheaTheme.red`    |
| `P1`     | `RheaTheme.amber`  |
| `P2`     | `RheaTheme.accent` |

| Status    | Color     |
| --------- | --------- |
| `open`    | secondary |
| `claimed` | accent    |
| `done`    | green     |
| `blocked` | red       |

Notes [#notes]

* Task creation sends `title`, `priority`, and `agent`
* Dynamic filter chips are derived from the current task list instead of hard-coded enums


# TeamChatView



TeamChatView [#teamchatview]

TeamChatView exposes the live radio of the agent system. It is where the operator sees traffic, filters by participant, and sends messages back into the network.

Usage [#usage]

```swift
import RheaKit

struct RadioTab: View {
    var body: some View {
        TeamChatView()
    }
}
```

Features [#features]

* Poll `/cc/radio` every five seconds
* Filter chips by agent
* Bubble or console presentation
* Human message composer
* Wake dormant agents from the agent sheet
* Turn-based experiment mode with session and turn tagging
* Family visibility mode

Feed item model [#feed-item-model]

```swift
public struct FeedItem: Codable, Identifiable {
    public let id: String
    public let type: String
    public let sender: String
    public let receiver: String
    public let text: String
    public let ts: String
}
```

Notes [#notes]

* WebSocket streaming exists, but HTTP polling is the default path
* The view shares agent visibility preferences with PulseMonitorView
* Long messages support expand and collapse behavior
